guide.title: Landmand: Golf in Homer, Nebraska
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking for Nebraska places Landmand third, and it is the highest-ranked entry on that fifteen-course list carrying Golf Digest's own "Public" access label: the two courses ranked above it, Sand Hills Golf Club (Mullen) at #1 and CapRock Ranch (Valentine) at #2, are each labelled Private. Landmand's own FAQ states, verbatim, "We do not currently offer memberships," which makes this the plainest public access in the fifty-state set. Architects Rob Collins and Tad King built the course; Golf Digest's review describes fairways 80 to 100 yards wide and greens that are, in the magazine's own words, "cumulatively and in some cases individually, the largest in the United States." The course sits off South Bluff Road in Dakota precinct, Dakota County, Nebraska, outside the incorporated limits of Homer village, though it takes a Homer, NE 68030 mailing address. The 2026 season, per the club's own FAQ, "opens on May 16th, 2026 & ends on October 1st, 2026."

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Landmand's mailing address is 2073 S. Bluff Rd., Homer, NE 68030. By road, Sioux City, Iowa is 14.3 miles from the course, and Sioux Gateway Airport (SUX) — also known as Brigadier General Bud Day Field, in Woodbury County, Iowa — is 16.8 miles away, both routes running by way of US 75/US 77. From Sioux City, the route runs south on US 75/US 77, then west on county roads — 210th Street, H Avenue and 212th Street — to South Bluff Road. Golf Digest's own review describes the course as being "about 10 miles from Sioux City, Iowa"; the routed distance to the city's downtown is 14.3 miles.

sections.heading: Booking a tee time
sections.body: Landmand's own FAQ states plainly, under "Do you offer memberships?": "We do not currently offer memberships." Tee times for the 2026 season run through ForeUp, and the 2027 season through Whoosh; a waitlist is also posted on the club's own site. Every tee time carries a $25 nonrefundable deposit per golfer: cancel more than a week out and the rest of the payment comes back, minus that $25; cancel inside a week and there is no refund at all. The club caps groups at two carts, does not allow fivesomes, and does not allow additional walkers added to a foursome; brokering or reselling a tee time through a third party is against club policy and can cost a golfer the reservation. On a wet morning the club offers push carts at no charge or a full refund, a call made the morning of play rather than before it. The 2026 Landmand golf season, per the club's FAQ: "The 2026 Landmand golf season opens on May 16th, 2026 & ends on October 1st, 2026." A round costs $160 per golfer with cart included, per the same FAQ page under its 2026 season heading; walking the round earns a first beer on the house, and the club does not offer a replay rate.

sections.heading: Landmand
sections.body: Rob Collins and Tad King designed Landmand. Golf Digest's review states that "the only way for architects Rob Collins and Tad King to make the golf look like it fit against the endless backdrops was to construct fairways 80 to 100 yards wide and greens that are, cumulatively and in some cases individually, the largest in the United States." Collins has described the site in his own words, on the club's homepage: "When we got up in the hills up there, it was really quite jaw-dropping. It's got a little bit of the Sand Hills look to it, it looks like a links course in Ireland or the Sandhills, it's just this very raw, natural, tumbling landscape." Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking for Nebraska places Landmand third, labelled "Public," with a previous rank also of third — the highest-ranked course on that list to carry the "Public" label, above #2 CapRock Ranch (Valentine) and #1 Sand Hills Golf Club (Mullen), both Private.

sections.heading: Staying near the course
sections.body: Landmand books cabins on site, direct, through its own Lodgify page, at $800 a night; cabin bookings do not include tee times. A cabin reservation carries a $60 nonrefundable deposit, with 90% of the remaining prepayment refundable at 21 days or more before arrival, 50% at 14 days, and none inside 14 days. Check-in is at 3:00 p.m., with the cabin's door code sent out at 2:00 p.m. that day. The club's own Farmer's Table food truck, on site, runs 7:15 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. per the FAQ, which adds that closing hours may change toward the end of the season. Off the course, the club's FAQ names the South Sioux City Marriott Riverfront — 385 East 4th Street, South Sioux City, NE 68776 — as offering golfers a discounted rate through a link on Landmand's own site. The hotel's live website currently returns an access error to automated requests, so this guide names the property and its address without claiming it is presently open for bookings or that the discount is currently honored.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Landmand?
faq.answer: Book through ForeUp for the 2026 season or Whoosh for the 2027 season, both linked from the club's own site; a waitlist is posted there too. Every tee time carries a $25 nonrefundable deposit per golfer, refunded in full minus that deposit if you cancel more than a week out, and not refunded at all inside a week. The 2026 season, per the club's own FAQ, "opens on May 16th, 2026 & ends on October 1st, 2026" — a hard close for anyone planning an autumn round.

faq.question: Do I need a membership to play?
faq.answer: No. Landmand's own FAQ states plainly, "We do not currently offer memberships." It is a daily-fee public course, and the highest-ranked course in Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Nebraska Best in State list to carry the magazine's "Public" label.

faq.question: Where is Landmand?
faq.answer: In Dakota precinct, Dakota County, Nebraska, off South Bluff Road — outside the incorporated limits of Homer village, though the course takes a Homer, NE 68030 mailing address. Sioux City, Iowa is 14.3 miles away by US 75/US 77, and Sioux Gateway Airport (SUX) is 16.8 miles away by the same route.

faq.question: What does a round cost?
faq.answer: $160 per golfer, cart included, per Landmand's own FAQ under its 2026 season heading. Walk the round and the club will buy the first beer; there is no replay rate.

faq.question: Where can I stay?
faq.answer: Landmand's own cabins, on site, at $800 a night, booked direct through the club's Lodgify page — cabin bookings do not include tee times. Off the course, the club's FAQ names the South Sioux City Marriott Riverfront, 385 East 4th Street, South Sioux City, NE 68776, as offering a discounted golfer rate. Its live website currently returns an access error to automated requests, so this guide makes no claim about whether that rate, or the hotel itself, is presently active.
